name: Cascading PostgreSQL Connection Pool Exhaustion
description: A cascading failure triggered by two factors: a connection leak bug in TaskRepository.findTasksWithCustomFilter() and a 10x spike in webhook traffic from a GitHub integration. Under normal load the leak is negligible, but the traffic spike caused the connection pool to exhaust, bringing down task-service and cascading into project-service and notification-service.

root_cause.summary: MULTI-CAUSE: (1) Connection leak in TaskRepositoryCustomImpl.findTasksWithCustomFilter() at lines 95-98 — when a SQLException occurs during ResultSet processing, the catch block throws a RuntimeException without closing the connection. The connection.close() at line 102-108 is outside the try-catch and is never reached on exception. (2) A spike in webhook traffic from a GitHub integration starting at 09:00 increased calls to findTasksWithCustomFilter() by 10x. Under normal load (~200 req/s) the leak rate was negligible because exceptions were rare. The webhook spike pushed request rate to ~800 req/s, triggering more filter-column edge cases and SQL errors, causing the leak rate to exceed HikariCP's pool recovery capacity.
root_cause.mechanism: The catch block at line 95 catches SQLException and throws RuntimeException at line 98. The connection variable, acquired at line 52, is only closed at lines 102-108 which are outside the try-catch block. When the RuntimeException propagates, connection.close() is never executed, leaking the connection back to HikariCP. Each leaked connection is held indefinitely. With 20 max pool connections and ~800 req/s hitting findTasksWithCustomFilter() via WebhookProcessor.processWebhook() (line 40-41), the pool exhausts within 30 minutes of the traffic spike.
root_cause.trigger: GitHub integration webhook spike starting at 09:00 on 2024-01-25. A customer connected a large GitHub organization with ~200 repositories, triggering batch webhook events for issue syncing. WebhookProcessor.processBatch() (line 56-66) parallelizes processing across 10 threads, each calling findTasksWithCustomFilter().
root_cause.why_not_caught: The connection leak bug was introduced in DEPLOY-TS-023 (v3.1.0, deployed 2024-01-22). Under normal webhook volume (~80 req/s), SQLExceptions in findTasksWithCustomFilter were rare (<1/hour) and leaked connections were reclaimed by HikariCP's leak detection before accumulating. The 10x traffic spike changed the failure mode from slow drip to rapid exhaustion.

red_herring.description: CPU spike on search-service at 09:45 caused by a scheduled re-indexing job processing 45,000 workspace documents. The re-index job runs daily and completed normally by 10:15. It has no dependency on task-service, project-service, or their databases. The timing coincidence with the cascade makes it look related but it is entirely independent.

cascade_path: task-service connection pool exhausts (09:45) -> task-service returns 503s
project-service calls task-service for task validation during project operations -> project-service starts failing (10:00)
notification-service depends on both task-service (task details) and project-service (project details) -> notification queue backs up (10:15)

args.title: Cascading failure — task-service connection pool exhaustion
